title: Jean Goldkette's band and Chauncey Morehouse in Detroit
summary: Moore remembers only Chauncey Morehouse from Goldkette's band, barely knew Goldkette, and did not know Trumbauer.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Well, you mentioned in our last session (and this is going back a bit) that in Detroit at the Graystone Ballroom, there was also the Jean Goldkette Band. Do you
remember any of the guys from that band? Do you remember Chauncey Morehouse?
Well, he's about the only one I remember in that band. Because I didn't know too many people in that band.
What was so special about Chauncey?

Well, I didn't have the opportunity to hear him play too much. I liked to be around him a whole lot and talk about different musicians, different things, you know. I was kind of young then, about as young then as I am now...
That was some fifty-five years ago.

Yes. I would like to get...always like to get in conversation with the top musicians. Because I was... I'd get a lot of experience by being around them, they'd talk their talk, you know... And they'd go way back. It's...
No. I think I met him once or twice. Because he was a busy man. He was always moving all the time, you know.
So he didn't leave much of an impression.
No. He... The little man didn't have... Nobody wrote about him, you know. Which I was... I didn't know too much...didn't know nothin' about him. Just heard about him
once or twice from the musicians. He didn't want to take up too much time with unknown musicians, you know. He had his hands full to try to keep his own thing going there; you know, different bands.
Yeah. I hear he had a pretty rough time.
Frankie Trumbauer was in that band, I believe.
Did you get a chance to know Frankie?
